case_name: Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. v Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr.
facts: The marriage of Jitendra Raghuvanshi (Appellant No.1 herein) and Babita Raghuvanshi, respondent-wife, was solemnized on 22.02.2002 as per Hindu rites and rituals.

After the marriage, the parties were residing together as husband and wife at District Baitul, M.P. On 05.03.2003, an FIR being No.172 of 2003 was registered at P.S. Sarni, Dist. Baitul for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 406 read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'the IPC') at the instance of Babita Raghuvanshi - respondent-wife owing to the harassment and torture meted out to her in the matrimonial home by her husband and his relatives.

During the pendency of the criminal proceedings, in the year 2012, with the help and intervention of family members, friends and well-wishers, the parties amicably settled their differences by way of mutual settlement. Pursuant thereto, on 03.04.2012, a compromise/settlement application was filed for dropping of the criminal proceedings in Criminal Case No.4166 of 2011 and FIR No.172 of 2003 dated 05.03.2003 before the trial Court.
Respondent-wife also filed an affidavit stating that she did not wish to pursue the criminal proceedings against the appellants.
issues: The scope and ambit of power u/s.482 of the Code has been examined by this Court in a catena of earlier decisions.

When such matters are resolved either by the wife agreeing to rejoin the matrimonial home or by mutual settlement of other pending disputes for which both the sides approached the High Court and jointly prayed for quashing of the criminal proceedings or the FIR or complaint by the wife under Sections 498A and 406 of IPC, whether the prayer can be declined on the sole ground that since the offences are non-compoundable u/s.320 of the Code, it would be impermissible for the Court to quash the criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants filed an application being M.CR.C. No.2877 of 2012 before the High Court invoking its inherent powers u/s.482 of the Code to quash the criminal proceedings launched against them.
The parties, in the instant case, arrived at a mutual settlement and the complainant also has sworn an affidavit supporting the stand of the appellants.

It is not in dispute that after filing of a complaint in respect of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 of IPC, the parties, in the instant case, arrived at a mutual settlement and the complainant also has sworn an affidavit supporting the stand of the appellants.
respondent_arguments: The respondent-wife filed an application being M.CR.C. No.2877 of 2012 before the High Court invoking its inherent powers u/s.482 of the Code to quash the criminal proceedings launched against her.
The respondent-wife also filed an affidavit stating that she did not wish to pursue the criminal proceedings against the appellants.
court_reasoning: This Court has upheld the powers of the High Court u/s.482 to quash criminal proceedings where dispute is of a private nature and a compromise is entered into between the parties who are willing to settle their differences amicably.
The inherent powers of the High Court u/s.482 of the Code are wide and unfettered.

Even if the offences are non-compoundable, if they relate to matrimonial disputes and the court is satisfied that the parties have settled the same amicably and without any pressure, we hold that for the purpose of securing ends of justice, S.320 of the Code would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing of FIR, complaint or the subsequent criminal proceedings.
The courts should be less hesitant in exercising its extraordinary jurisdiction.
holding: We set aside the impugned judgment of the High Court dated 04.07.2012 passed in M.CR.C. No.2877 of 2012 and quash the proceedings in Criminal Case No.4166 of 2011.
